independent_semantics.kind: POSIX signal-mask specification reasoning; not native runtime evidence
independent_semantics.rule: For zero sa_flags, SIGUSR1 handler entry adds sa_mask (SIGUSR2) and the delivered signal SIGUSR1 to the caller mask; normal signal return restores the saved caller mask.
payload_observations: Handler sees SIGUSR2 blocked and increments handled exactly once.
After raise returns, SIGUSR1 and SIGUSR2 membership match their respective baseline membership.
limitations: Automatic SIGUSR1 blocking inside the handler is required by the specification but is not inspected by this frozen payload.

Exact restoration of arbitrary mask members is not proved: only SIGUSR1 and SIGUSR2 are compared. The checked-in oracle's broad relational assertion and unresolved-expectations field remain unchanged and cannot establish formal acceptance.

Baseline is queried rather than normalized. SIGUSR1 must initially be unblocked for synchronous handling; SIGUSR2 must initially be unblocked to make the observed_blocked bit evidence of augmentation.
No nesting, SA_NODEFER, SA_RESETHAND, alternate stack, multithreaded delivery, nonlocal handler exit or pending-signal ordering is tested.
The unused required set is initialized but never used; it adds no coverage.

cheap_regression.profile: Python only; no compiler, Docker, root, network or payload execution; 1 CPU/1 GiB planning share; under 120 seconds
checks: Frozen payload and oracle hashes and exact expected stream bytes.
Independent set-rule model across eight baseline combinations and explicit whole-mask-restoration counterexample.
Synthetic collector report satisfies the existing evaluator only as PROTOCOL_PASS with all acceptance/execution booleans false.
Evaluator rejects missing newline, nonempty stderr, nonzero exit, signal death, retained procfs, missing EOF, truncation and wrong argv.
Evaluator rejects missing actual route, retirement, process release or procfs deletion markers, missing QMP shutdown and uncertain teardown.
